proof_roadmap: Reduction to the local case (proof lines 3611-3612).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the local ring of an absolutely integrally closed ring at a prime is strictly henselian. The proof first reduces, using the behaviour of the property under quotients and localisations, to the case where the ring is local and the prime is its maximal ideal. There the residue field is algebraically closed by the same reduction, and every monic polynomial over the ring decomposes completely into linear factors, which is precisely the condition in the definition of a henselian (indeed strictly henselian) ring, so the definition applies directly.
